checks.finding: AC-030 (requirements.md:86) instructs that the push step state the push-failure rule 'in all three of its parts,' and enumerates exactly three (requirements.md:88-90): (1) failure does not change consent state, (2) the agent reports the failure, (3) a same-scope retry proceeds without a new consent prompt, re-entering at the pre-upload check point. TEST-051's Test Matrix one-liner (acceptance-tests.md:61) mirrors those same three items. But TEST-051's Test Details (acceptance-tests.md:248) adds a requirement with no anchor in AC-030's text: 'As with TEST-043, the assertion must also find the boundary statement: a push failure is not AC-019's persistent "not permitted" outcome and writes no standing forbiddance.' Contrast sibling AC-026 (requirements.md:56-64), whose distinguish-from-AC-019 clause is its own explicit enumerated part 3 ('the decline is explicitly distinguished from the persistent "not permitted" outcome of AC-019', requirements.md:62), matched 1:1 by TEST-043 (acceptance-tests.md:53, :216). AC-030 has no equivalent fourth part. An implementer satisfying AC-030's stated 'three parts' would reasonably conclude the push-failure text is complete; a verifier building TEST-051 from its Test Details narrative would require a fourth, textually ungrounded statement, so the identical skill edit could satisfy AC-030 as written while failing TEST-051 as detailed. This is an internal inconsistency between requirements.md's AC text and acceptance-tests.md's own test-detail narrative, present before any design or implementation choice is made, so it belongs to spec review rather than a later gate. Major, per the calibration's classification rule, because it is a scope-definition ambiguity that will cause a downstream mismatch, not a workflow-safety contradiction.

No direct conflict found. AC-030's rationale (requirements.md:92) explicitly reconciles the push-failure rule with AC-028's explicit-withdrawal model ('treating a failed push as an implicit revocation would collide with AC-028's explicit-withdrawal model -- withdrawal is the only way a consent is meant to stop applying mid-session'). Part 3's 'without a new consent prompt' (requirements.md:90) does not conflict with AC-026 branch 2's re-prompt-on-next-attempt (requirements.md:61-62; acceptance-tests.md:52) because the two describe different triggers: AC-026 concerns a still-unresolved consent request answered 'no'; AC-030 concerns a technical push failure occurring only after consent was already granted (push happens after the consent step per REQ-003's stated flow order, requirements.md:132). Reviewed REQ-001 through REQ-008, Non-goals, and Baseline Constraints for conflicting pairs and found none that directly contradict. The AC-030/TEST-051 discrepancy is an incompleteness/scope-definition gap (captured under AMBIGUITY), not a stated conflict between two assertions of fact.

The push-failure edge case -- previously unspecified and flagged by impl-review round-2 reviewers (requirements.md:92, 'after impl review's round-2 reviewers independently found the behaviour unspecified') -- is now covered by AC-030/TEST-051 (requirements.md:84-95; acceptance-tests.md:61, 246-248), bringing it in line with sibling negative-path coverage already present for the persistent not-permitted outcome (AC-019/TEST-028-030), transient decline (AC-026/TEST-041-043), and mid-session withdrawal (AC-028/TEST-046-047). Edge Cases 1-9 (requirements.md:271-281) each already map to a resolved OQ/REQ/AC/TEST per the document's own tracking. No additional material negative path, boundary state, or failure mode implied by the push-failure addition was found uncovered.

AC-030 introduces no new bare, unconditional claim about shared, git-tracked state; its illustrative push-failure causes (network error, timeout, auth expiry, service outage -- requirements.md:88) are generic categories, not file:line assertions about repository state requiring re-verification. The document's existing shared-state claims (BL-004/BL-005 protected-file membership, the ADR sequence, the CI registration surface) already carry explicit re-verification instructions (requirements.md:286-288, 297-298) and are unaffected by this edit. Remaining Open Questions (OQ-6, OQ-7, OQ-9, OQ-10; requirements.md:317-321, 332-336) are each explicitly marked non-blocking and hedged by a named acceptance criterion that accepts the gap rather than guessing (AC-005 for OQ-6, AC-010 for OQ-7, AC-018 for OQ-9; OQ-10 explicitly owned by security-spec.md and stated to touch no criterion in this document).

This feature's subject is a human-consent egress boundary, so the check is in scope (not SKIP). The boundary is testable throughout: first-upload gating (AC-001/TEST-001), the three-valued consent-resolution outcome including denial (AC-019/TEST-028-030), transient decline (AC-026/TEST-041-043), mid-session withdrawal (AC-028/TEST-046-047), destination binding (AC-027/TEST-044-045), and now push-failure non-revocation (AC-030/TEST-051; requirements.md:84-95). The one soft spot -- whether TEST-051 requires a fourth 'boundary statement' beyond AC-030's stated three parts (see AMBIGUITY) -- does not by itself make the approval boundary untestable; some testable form of the push-failure rule is unambiguously required and present in both requirements.md and acceptance-tests.md.

The product decision behind AC-030 (push failure does not revoke consent; the failure is reported; retry proceeds without re-prompting) is fully decided by the human with an explicit rationale (requirements.md:92, dated 2026-08-05), so a design reviewer does not need to invent the underlying behaviour. TEST-051 is packaged as a single Test Matrix row (acceptance-tests.md:61) rather than one row per part -- a deviation from this document's dominant convention of one row per independently-failable part (used for AC-001, AC-003, AC-013, AC-021, AC-026, AC-027, AC-028, AC-029) despite AC-030 using the same 'vacuous-satisfaction' rationale (requirements.md:94) that motivates that convention elsewhere -- but the Test Details narrative (acceptance-tests.md:246-248) is explicit enough about the three independently-checked failure shapes that a downstream test author is not left to invent verification structure. This stylistic deviation does not clear the bar for a FAIL on its own; the more substantive scope gap it points at is already captured under AMBIGUITY.
